title: School completion, Eastern and South-eastern Asia, by wealth
headline: In E. and S.-E. Asia, primary completion for all by 2030 needs the rate to keep rising 0.3 points a year
subtitle: Percentage of a cohort of children or young people aged 3-5 years above the intended age for the last grade of primary education who have completed primary education
years: So far it has risen 0.3 points a year, from 90.1% in 2000 to 98.1% in 2024.
data_line: Data: UNESCO UIS via UN SDG Global Database, series SE_TOT_CPLR, extracted 1 Nov 2026
flags: headline at 52 px: no candidate fits two lines at 56 px
alt: In E. and S.-E. Asia, primary completion for all by 2030 needs the rate to keep rising 0.3 points a year. So far it has risen 0.3 points a year, from 90.1% in 2000 to 98.1% in 2024. Children completing primary school, Eastern and South-eastern Asia: 90.1% in 2000, 98.1% in 2024. At that pace about 100.0% in 2030; reaching 100% needs 0.3 points a year.
method: Method: linear pace, 2000 to 2024; target year 2030.
question: Where has primary completion moved at anything like 0.3 points a year, and what made it possible?
